claims.head: Like for like: Robinson vs. Greene

claims.head: Expect the Hurricanes to have the puck more
claims.body: The Hurricanes have been the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Hurricanes to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

notes.text: Bowen Byram is day to day (upper-body injury) and has missed the last 7 games. He is a top-pair defenseman. Wyatt Kaiser has taken his spot beside Artyom Levshunov. That pair has had 34% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 80:55 together, down from 47% with Byram.

Taylor Hall is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 8 games. Nikolaj Ehlers has taken his spot beside Logan Stankoven and Jackson Blake. That line has had 83% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 66:02 together, up from 60% with Hall.
Jordan Staal is out 1-2 months (calf tear) and has missed the last 10 games. Mark Jankowski has taken his spot beside Jordan Martinook and Nikolaj Ehlers.

Alexander Nikishin is out (not injury related) and has missed the last 8 games. Juuso Välimäki has taken his spot beside Shayne Gostisbehere. That pair has had 77% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 69:28 together.
Logan Stankoven has started killing penalties: on the ice for 26% of the team’s shorthanded time in 16 games, up from 1% last season.

stakes: The Blackhawks go in eighth in the Central with 9 points, the Hurricanes first in the NHL with 26 points.

CAR.body: Carolina has been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and has home-ice advantage. The Blackhawks’ best way in is getting good looks.

story.head: The Hurricanes come in hot
paras: The Hurricanes won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-2 in Chicago on Oct 10. The Hurricanes have won four straight, the last a 7-0 rout of Winnipeg. The Blackhawks (4-9-1) lost 5-4 in overtime to Boston on Oct 31. Going in, the Hawks are last in the Central (31st in the NHL) and the Hurricanes are first in the NHL.

The Blackhawks have played better than their record (.321) says: their chances are worth about .384, and their finishing has held them back. The Hurricanes’ record (.812) is about what their chances are worth.

The Blackhawks pick their shots (2nd lowest) and don't block many shots (32nd). They also have struggled on the power play (31st), so their struggling power play gets a tough test from the Hurricanes’ penalty killers. Chicago has scored 2.21 goals a game, the second fewest in the league, and allowed 3.79, the third most. As for the Hurricanes, they take away shots from the point (lowest) and create more chances on the penalty kill than anyone (1st), but give up a lot of dangerous shots (32nd). Carolina has scored 3.94 goals a game, the third most in the league, and allowed 2.19, the second fewest. The Hurricanes are likely to get plenty of pucks to the net against the Blackhawks.

Connor Bedard (4 G / 5 A / 9 P in 8 GP) leads the Blackhawks in scoring, and Roman Kantserov (5 G / 2 A / 7 P in 14 GP) has a team-high five goals. Sebastian Aho (9 G / 12 A / 21 P in 16 GP) leads the Hurricanes in scoring and is tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Logan Stankoven (10 G / 5 A / 15 P in 16 GP) has a team-high ten goals, tied for sixth in the NHL.
Spencer Knight (4-7-0 / .897 SV% in 11 GS) is in line to start for Chicago. Pyotr Kochetkov (10-0-0 / .929 SV% in 10 GS) has been a rock in net for Carolina and will likely start.

At home, Rod Brind'Amour likes to send Robinson, Kotkaniemi and Deslauriers out against opponents’ fourth lines, so watch for them against Smith, Greene and Greenway. Elsewhere, the Hurricanes usually control more of the chances than the Blackhawks do.

The Blackhawks have been without Bowen Byram since Oct 13.
The Hurricanes have been without Taylor Hall, Jordan Staal and Alexander Nikishin for several games.
